turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Hi. Well, I came in today because I keep getting these... nagging thoughts that I forgot something important. It's usually about things like worrying I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or maybe that I didn't set up my classroom materials safely for my students. And the frustrating part is, even when I know I probably handled it just fine, the doubt just keeps popping back into my head anyway.

symptom_reasoning.S065: The patient describes persistent, intrusive nagging doubts about whether they made mistakes with medication or classroom safety that repeatedly pop back into their head despite knowing they handled things fine, matching obsessions (pathological doubt).

turns.doctor_question: Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking things over and over or trying to neutralize the thoughts in some way?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. Um, before I leave the house or my classroom, I’ll usually go back over the same things a few times. I'll check the pill organizer, the stove, my lesson plans... or sometimes I just silently replay what I did in my head to make sure I did it right. I basically just keep checking until I feel calm enough to actually move on. It's pretty frustrating because doing all that makes me run late sometimes.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient describes engaging in repetitive checking behaviors (pill organizer, stove, lesson plans) and mental rituals (silently replaying actions) until feeling calm enough to move on, consistent with compulsions.

turns.doctor_question: When you have these nagging thoughts, do you feel driven to perform certain behaviors or mental acts to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce your anxiety?
turns.patient_response:
Yeah, that's pretty much exactly what I was just describing with the checking. When those thoughts hit me, I feel like I absolutely have to go back and look at the pill organizer or my desk at school, just to make sure nothing bad is going to happen. 

Doing that, or replaying my steps in my head, is really the only way to get that anxious feeling to go down so I can move on. But... yeah, it's really just the checking routines I just mentioned. I don't think I do anything else besides that.

symptom_reasoning.S066: The patient clearly describes feeling compelled to perform checking rituals and mental acts (replaying steps in their head) to relieve anxiety and prevent harm.
